propositions: Duplicate CAS push-retry-fetch-merge loops across workflows are consolidated into a single Python core module that owns retry budget, fetch-and-merge recovery, and delivery semantics.

The strict-mode push entrypoint raises typed PushDeliveryError with failure reason and unpushed-commit count; the Python adapter translates core failures to stderr and nonzero exit without calling sys.exit.
The locked commit-and-push entrypoint stages, commits, and delivers in a single transaction, with dirty-tree handling and bot identity/subject preservation.
Workflow adapters delegate delivery once through strict Python entrypoints; legacy library, CLI, MCP, and importer callers retain best-effort defaults with keyword-only strict=False.
No persisted schema or event vocabulary changed; rollback requires restoring previous workflow blocks before reverting the strict adapter and core entrypoints.
